“My love! How many eggs do you lay during your mating season?" The blue octopus asked enthusiastically, the forget-me-not eyes shining as it gazed at the figure before it, a red mermaid with strawberry blonde hair and red tips. The mermaid looked at him with an expression that was difficult to explain in the mermaid world.

But in human language, we could say that he was embarrassed and angry.

The story is quite simple: Mydei, the mermaid prince of the kingdom of Kremnos, is courted by a foreign octopus named Phainon. Actually, his name is Khaslana, but Phainon means ‘white calamity’ in the ancient Kremnoan language, the second name stuck well with the inhabitants of the kingdom.

Everyone started calling him Phainon, but Mydei still prefers to call him 'stupid octopus' or 'tuna deliverer’. Because he once released an entire school of tuna from the prince's trap.

"You... really dare to ask me something like that?!" Mydei finally asked, anger in his voice and disgust on his face, Phainon merely nodded.

"Of course, my dear! I need to know so that when we mate I can take care of the eggs with..." Mydei's eyes widened at Phainon's response, and he quickly interrupted with a laugh.

“Wait, wait... you," Mydei pointed at Phainon, "mate," pointed to himself, "with me?" The octopus quickly agreed, while two of his blue tentacles formed into a heart shape. 

"NEVER!"

‘never’, ‘ever’, ‘ver…’ The shrill voice uttering the sentence echoed across the ocean, a sound that could surely rival the song of a blue whale. Phainon undid the heart shape formed by its tentacles, and his enthusiastic expression vanished, replaced by a hurt one. Mydei quickly moved away from him, massaging his throat with the same hand that had pointed at the octopus.

"But my love…” he said, almost whimpering.

“ ’My love’, my tail! Get away from me or I'll rip all your tentacles off! HKS.” Phainon tried to protest, but as soon as he opened his mouth, a pair of red fins slapped him in the face. When he realized what was happening, he saw his prince swimming away, far from him.

That was the fifth rejection, and it was only Tuesday.

Phainon simply swam to the first large rock it saw to sit down and settle its tentacles, while smoothing the skin that had been brutally (hyperbole) wounded by beautiful fins.

‘'When the sea is he finally going to realize that he loves me too?” Phainon thought as he gazed at the corals in front of him.

Currently, Phainon has already been rejected 16,425 times by Mydei. Octopuses are intelligent, so Phainon knew how to calculate all the confessions he made to Mydei every day for three years.

But how could he not fall in love with the most handsome prince he had ever seen, the one who made him leave everything in the south to go and love him? Regardless of whether he was a prince, a wizard, or simply a warrior. He was his Mydei.

Phainon would never forget that day three years ago; he remembered it like it was yesterday. It was the time when the mermaids of Kremnos traveled south during mating season.

Phainon was returning to snoop around a sunken ship he had found the previous day; there was so much stuff that he had to leave some behind.

When he arrived back on the ship, there it was, a bright red figure that stood out against all the gold and purple and yellow vases.

The mermaid was fiddling with some gold coins and quickly dropped them as soon as he saw Phainon stand in front of him. Mydei didn't know what to do, whether to talk to the octopus, run away, or throw one of those vases at his head.

But for Phainon, the world had stopped; he could only notice the single braid in that golden hair, the feline eyes, and the bright red tail adorned with gold ornaments. How lucky, besides being a beautiful mermaid, he liked to collect treasures.

Phainon smiled and said, "hi! Did you like what you found here?" and Mydei simply nodded without saying anything. Silence returned.

Phainon tilted his head in question, but still, he wanted at least to hear the enchanting figure's voice, "I am Khaslana, and you, who are you?" 

Phainon tries to approach, and at the same pace, Mydei moves away. "Mydeimos, I'm Kremnoan,” Phainon raised his eyebrows in surprise.

“Wow, really? I've always wanted to go to Castrum Kremnos, they say they have the best sea warriors and the best tuna dishes, is that true?" Unfortunately, Mydei had not only become Phainon's first love, but also the object of his interest. Because for a common octopus from the coast of Aedes Elysiae, Castrum Kremnos was everything.

"Yeah, kind of like that." Mydei replied directly, after all, he was a little uncomfortable. Phainon interpreted Mydei's unease as a 'desire to sit down', so he swam to the upper deck of the ship.

“Come, Mydeimos!" Mydei followed him, and indeed, they sat down on the mast that was still standing of that shipwrecked vessel. 

“The Kremnoans always come here to mate, are you one of them, Mydeimos?" Mydei shook his head and looked down at his fins. Phainon was too close and he didn't want to keep staring at those tentacles. Or for the abdomen, which only had a blue and yellow cloak covering a small part of it.

“No... I only came because my comrades said it would be good for me to travel. I'll return to Kremnos before everyone else since I don't have anyone to call a partner." One of Phainon's hearts nearly leaped out of his chest, and he simply sighed.

“What a shame..." he was happy, "How's Kremnos, is it nice there?" 

“I can say yes. I have my friends, my mentors, and the hunting grounds are quite extensive; it's fun," aside from having grueling classes, having to reject suitors, or fighting against other kingdoms of the sea. 

“Mydeimos, are you a soldier?" Phainon looked him up and down, noticing mainly the symmetrical lines that flowed across the mermaid's human torso. It was beautiful. “I heard that only soldiers have those tattoos.”

Mydei looked at his abdomen and then at his arms, specifically at the tattoos, "Actually, they're marks that confirm the legitimacy of the royal family; soldiers only get tattoos as a tribute." After carefully examining his tattoos, he looked at Phainon, and smirks.

Phainon thought.

For one, two, three, four, five seconds. Until the two strands of his silver hair got scared and his jaw dropped.

"What!? You're from the royal family?!" Phainon was in shock. And with that, he saw Mydei let out a small giggle.

The most beautiful little laugh the sea has ever seen. pink lips parting slightly, revealing sharp little teeth along with fangs that were barely visible, but Phainon noticed. And damn, he hopes Mydei doesn't notice how flushed he is now.

“I'm not going to have your head cut off or ask you to kiss my fins or anything like that, don't worry." Mydei didn't need to worry, Phainon was willing to kiss his fins even if he wasn't ordered to.

“Well..." Phainon was a little shocked, but it's alright, it's not every day you find out that the one who's going to carry your eggs is a prince, "What were you doing here on the ship, Mydeimos?"

“Just call me Mydei.”

“Fine, Mydei!”

"I... just wanted to get away from the crowds for a bit. Sometimes mermaids lose their heads when they're about to mate, and I didn't want any misfortune."

“Oh... I understand."

It was understandable; after all, fertilizing the prince's eggs would guarantee a good life for anyone who dared, even if it wasn't consensual. 

The octopus and the mermaid sat on the mast of the sunken ship without exchanging another word.

In the following days, Mydei and Phainon would meet by chance, mainly when Mydei found it a good idea to explore abandoned ships to alleviate the boredom of being the only mermaid who did not participate in mating courtship.

And on the last day of the mating season, Mydei was preparing to go with his comrades, until Phainon grabbed him by the wrist and declared: "I... I'm going with you to Castrum Kremnos!" Phainon sighed, paused, and shame took over his expression, "May I?" The octopus smiled awkwardly, and without hesitation, Mydei took Phainon with him to Castrum Kremnos.

And after that day, Mydei had no peace of mind. A week later, Mydei discovered the octopus’s feelings for him. And Mydei, being a prince who was too busy, rejected him.

But octopuses are known for not giving up on their partners so easily, so for the past three years, Phainon has tried everything to win Mydei's heart. But in the end… He was met with shouts, insults, and had some tentacles ripped off for being too stubborn.

Phainon was still sitting on the rock when, by chance, his gaze lifted and he found Mydei swimming... out of the water? But hadn't Mydei gone the other way? What was his beloved planning this time?

Like a good octopus concerned for his beloved, he decided to get up and follow Mydei slowly, sneaking among the rocks in case it could camouflage himself. And so he did, Mydei had a very good spider-sense for a mermaid, constantly looking behind him, stopping to look around as well. Phainon already wanted to dye his hair gray so that he can camouflage himself among the rocks.

He saw Mydei emerge from the water and swim slowly towards the shore, stopping in front of enormous rocks that were just a few meters from the sand. The mermaid shake his head to remove the water from his hair, and although it was a very beautiful and extravagant scene, the octopus had to be on alert. Mydei fixed his hair, adjusted his braids, and positioned himself perfectly on the rock—just in case his tail hurt—and then began to pay attention to the beach ahead, as if he were waiting for something… or someone?

Phainon prayed to Phagousa with all his might that his thoughts about what Mydei wanted on the surface would dissipate... Or else the water level would rise about two meters from how much Phainon would cry if he was right.  No, it was impossible, Mydei had never shown attention to any mermaid, why a human?

Enough, Khaslana!

On the other side, Mydei waited anxiously, unaware that he was being followed.

Mydei didn't have to wait long before he heard footsteps on the sand, slow footsteps. The mermaid's gaze fell upon the silhouette that was near him, the source of those footsteps. Gradually, the silhouette revealed itself to be a girl with lavender hair, elf ears, and clothes considered to be those of a 'peasant'; she was holding a straw basket with a purple ribbon on the handle.

Mydei grinned from ear to ear, showing his canines and pointed teeth. The girl returned the smile, and then began to run. When she reached the water's edge, she took off her shoes to return to running. She went up to the group of rocks where the mermaid was, sat down, "hi, Mydei! Did I take too long?"

Mydei shook his head, relaxing his watchful stance on the rock, "I just arrived, how are things in Okhema, Castorice?" After asking, he took another look around the beach, "Where's Cipher?"

“Cipher will be a while because she said she's going to the market" Castorice paused to open the basket she was holding, then took out a red pomegranate. Mydei's pupils widened a little after they saw the shining fruit.

Castorice placed the pomegranate in Mydei's hands, and with her sharp claws, the mermaid effortlessly opened the fruit and began to savor the seeds. "In Okhema, all is well! It's the season for offerings of good harvest, the temples will be very full."

“I see..." Mydei and Castorice stopped talking, partly because the mermaid was focused on tasting the pomegranate, and Castorice took a sketchbook and a pencil from the same basket where she kept the fruits.

The silence was short-lived, because, as if he had fallen from the sky, Cipher appeared like a bolt of lightning, sitting next to, no, on the same rock as Castorice, and adding; the rock was quite small for two people. Mydei should have been startled by Cipher's immediate appearance, but he was quite used to it. Castorice frowned at having lost a comfortable spot. 

“Hello! Little Fish, Homebody princess?”

“Was the market really that crowded?" Mydei asked bluntly, finishing his first pomegranate. He held out his hand to Castorice, who quickly placed another fruit in his hand. 

“Yes! But it was for a good reason," after that, she picked up her bag and started searching for something inside. When she found what she was looking for, the cat's eyes glowed, "Aha! I found it!"

With her index finger and thumb, she showed Mydei a triangular gold earring, "take it! It's for you." Mydei frowned, and put his hand down to take the gold earring and he examined it closely. He held the jewel up to his eyes and came to a conclusion, "The earring is beautiful... but it's missing the jewel."

The triangular shape had a round hollow, where there was clearly a diamond or some other precious stone.

And that's how their friendship worked. Mydei would sometimes bring treasures from the sea for both Cipher and Castorice, and the girls would bring treasures from the land or just food that Mydei never would see underwater.

Castorice saw him and, in an act of desperation, began throwing her own water canteen on top of him. Mydei's pale tail regained its color after feeling the water on its gills. He saw his savior was just as frightened as he was, almost crying. 

As a token of gratitude, Mydei promised to form an alliance with Castorice, and so they began trading things from the sea for things from humans.

“What!?" they said in unison, and with a loud voice, which made Mydei's ear fins vibrate in disapproval at the intonation.

Castorice made a saddened expression; after all, if the word 'prince' was in this story, she quickly thought it was about her ancestors.

They would give a pearl the same color as the tail of their loved one, and then they would get married, and they would use the pearl in some wedding adornment and things like that." Cipher's eyes seemed to sparkle at the story, and on the other side, Castorice remained quiet.
